title: Some Interesting Curses
summary: Silly episode on interesting curses. Covers the curse of Brunswick Springs in Brunswick, Vermont (Abenaki legend, French soldier, 1894 and 1929-1931 hotel fires, later land bought back by the Abenaki and placed in trust); the Curse of It Took, the Hollywood script based on Mordecai Richler's novel The Incomparable Atuk, linked to deaths of Belushi, Sam Kennison, John Candy, Michael O'Donoghue and Chris Farley; the Curse of Tamerlane, where Stalin's 1941 disinterment of Timur's tomb was followed by Operation Barbarossa and a curse that appears to be a 2003 invention; the Curse of the Billy Goat, William Sianis and Murphy the goat barred from Wrigley Field in 1945, lifted in 2016; and the Jackie Chan endorsement curse. Ends with a listener mail about the Donut King documentary and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter on curses
segments.summary: Hosts joke about whether the show is cursed, past TV appearances that supposedly led to cancellations, and set up the episode as an anthropological look at curses, mostly legend.

segments.title: Curse of Brunswick Springs
segments.summary: The six mineral springs in Brunswick, Vermont, sacred to the Abenaki. A French soldier is said to have been healed there; he later bottled the water, a fight followed, and a widow cursed anyone who tries to profit from the springs. A resort later burned repeatedly, and the Abenaki eventually sold the land to Vermont, where it is held in trust.

segments.title: Transition to Hollywood
segments.summary: Brief transition from Brunswick to the Hollywood curse of Atuk.

segments.title: Curse of Atuk in Hollywood
segments.summary: Mordecai Richler's 1963 satirical novel The Incomparable Atuk, its Hollywood adaptation attempts, and the deaths tied to the project: John Belushi, Sam Kennison (whose film was halted by a lawsuit), John Candy, Michael O'Donoghue, and Chris Farley. The hosts discuss the book's publication timing and the Confederacy of Dunces, which was also repeatedly attached to actors who died.

segments.title: Holmes and Watson aside
segments.summary: Hosts give a plug for the Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly film Holmes and Watson, and discuss the word foible.

segments.title: Curse of Timur the Lame
segments.summary: Timur (Tamerlane), a fourteenth-century Mongol conqueror blamed for about seventeen million deaths. He died in 1405 and was entombed in Samarkand until Stalin ordered his exhumation in 1941. Two days later Germany invaded the USSR, and Stalin reportedly reburied him. The supposed curse inscription appears to have been invented around 2003 and is not on the tomb per the Soviet team's translation.

segments.title: Curse of the Billy Goat
segments.summary: In October 1945, William Sianis and his goat Murphy were refused entry to Wrigley Field during World Series Game four, reportedly because the goat stank. Sianis cursed the Cubs, who then lost the series to the Tigers. Later attempts to lift the curse with Murphy's descendants in 1973 and other years failed, and the curse was reportedly lifted in 2016 when Sianis rang the Traveling Bell during Game seven.

segments.title: Transition to Jackie Chan
segments.summary: Brief transition introducing Jackie Chan and his Western films.

segments.title: Jackie Chan endorsement curse
segments.summary: The supposed curse on brands that hire Jackie Chan as a pitchman, with examples of companies that failed or had problems, and the Australian Open 2025 players who lost after meeting him. The hosts suggest this is largely statistical given how many endorsements he does.

segments.title: Closing curse tease
segments.summary: Hosts tease an unnamed final curse called the zero factor and mention the Wayback Machine needs a tune-up.

segments.title: Listener mail on the Donut King
segments.summary: Listener Brett recommends the documentary The Donut King about a Cambodian immigrant who used a donut shop to help bring families to the US, following a prior episode on Vietnamese nail salons. Hosts invite listener suggestions.
